rows.figure: 13-15 drownings a year, average (official statement, period not stated)
rows.scope: Average number of drownings per year in New Hampshire as stated by the NH Department of Safety in an August 2020 water-safety release. The release does not state the averaging period, the data source (OCME, vital records or Marine Patrol), whether all intents or accidental only, whether boating (water transport) deaths are included, or whether residents or deaths occurring in the state are counted. No split by water body or activity. Not a yearly count: the same release adds 'So far this year, New Hampshire has had seven drownings' (as of 7 Aug 2020).
rows.source: New Hampshire Department of Safety, news release 'Be Safe When Enjoying New Hampshire Waters', posted 7 August 2020 (joint message with State Police Marine Patrol, Fish and Game and the Department of Natural and Cultural Resources)
rows.do_not_add_to: A rounded average from a press statement, not a tabulated count: do not add to the Maine OCME rows, to us-cdc-4345 or any US total, to uscg-boating-2024, or to each other across years; do not use as a denominator for rates; replace with CDC WONDER or OCME yearly counts when found and keep this row only as the state's own statement.
rows.note: Grade C: an organisation's own statement with no table behind it. Corroborated in wording by an NHPR article of the same date quoting a Fish and Game colonel ('averages 13 to 15 deadly drownings a year'). No official per-year count for New Hampshire was found; see notes.

notes: Status partial: no official per-year count of drowning deaths for New Hampshire was found through the routes reachable here, so the acceptance checks (one row per year, latest five years) are not met. The single row is the state's own rounded average ('13-15 drownings every year', NH Department of Safety, August 2020), grade C, with no table behind it. What exists but was out of reach: (1) CDC WONDER, Underlying Cause of Death, New Hampshire, ICD-10 W65-W74 plus V90 and V92, 2018-2023 (suppression applies below 10 deaths per cell, so an all-ages state total should be shown but age or sex splits may be suppressed); (2) CDC WISQARS Fatal Injury Reports, drowning, New Hampshire; (3) the NH DHHS Health WISDOM 'Injury Prevention Dashboard' (wisdom.dhhs.nh.gov), which may carry a drowning mortality indicator by year; (4) USCG Recreational Boating Statistics Table 32 (five-year deaths by state) for a boating-only count, 2024 edition p. 64 (all boating deaths, not drownings only). The NH OCME's only public statistical report found (Biennial Report 2017-2019) tabulates manner of death and opioid deaths, not drowning; a person could ask the OCME (doj.nh.gov/medical-examiner) whether later biennial reports or a drowning tabulation exist. Child-only official figures seen, not recorded as rows because they are pooled and age-restricted: NH DHHS Child Fatality Review 2023 gives drowning as 8.1% of unintentional injury deaths at ages 1-21, 2018-2022; the NH Violence and Injury Prevention Plan (2020) gives 18 drowning deaths of NH children and teens aged 0-19 in 2009-2018 plus seven out-of-state youths drowned in NH in that period. Press corroboration only: NHPR (7 Aug 2020) quotes a Fish and Game colonel giving the same 13-to-15-a-year average. Alcohol-involved recreational boating deaths in NH per USCG Table 8 (2024 edition, p. 26-27): 0 (2020), 2 (2021), 0 (2022), 0 (2023), 1 (2024); a contributing-factor subset, not a setting split, so not recorded as rows. For contrast, the Maine bundle (state-counts-maine) found the Maine OCME annual reports printing drowning mode-of-death counts by year; New Hampshire's OCME has no equivalent public series that search could reach.
